findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

I found no blocking errors. The audit-projection policy fails closed. If any tracked file outside `.project/`, `plugin/` and `packages/cli/codex-plugin/` changes, the hash no longer matches the shipped policy, so projection turns off and the audit tickets and summary are bound in full. `requireCleanInputs` checks cleanliness before `sourceIdentity` reads working-tree bytes, so a dirty reader cannot spoof the shipped hash. When the root and the clone disagree (for example, a mode-only edit to an audit ticket), the identity comparison refuses the run. Projection removes only the Work Log section and the phase, status and timestamp fields. All other frontmatter and body text stays bound. The new controls distinguish the cases they claim: the extensionless loaded-reader case, paired executable-mode checks, private dependency copies, and external runtime and native package metadata going stale. The docs state the conservative fallback and the limit that generated bundles are trusted. The main weakness is that "reader code is unchanged since review" rests on a hash that people refresh by hand. It does not prove the audit outputs are never loaded. That is a policy that was reviewed and documented, so I list it as a warning.

The audit exemption depends on a reviewed hash (`audit-readers.json` `source_sha256`), not on observing what the run actually loads. The positive control in `bounded-observation-runtime.node.ts` tells the developer to 'refresh the shipped identity' whenever any reader or doc changes. If someone adds code that reads the observer audit summary or a ticket's Work Log and then refreshes the hash mechanically, the exemption comes back while the output is a loaded input. The plan says 'Any listed output actually loaded by execution is byte-bound', but the code only guarantees 'reader code unchanged since the last refresh'. The website doc describes the limit honestly. Consider requiring a review receipt, or a negative control that greps the fixed-lane sources for the audit paths, before a refresh is accepted.

`auditReaderIdentity` excludes all of `.project/`, `plugin/` and `packages/cli/codex-plugin/`. Generated bundles (exercised by `catalogue.test.ts` and `codex-plugin-version.test.ts`) and any data-driven configuration under `.project/` could cause a run to read the audit summary or a Work Log without turning projection off. Their bytes are still fully bound in `sourceIdentity`, so a change to them still makes the observation stale. The gap is only the exemption itself. The docs cover this for the generated bundles but not for files under `.project/`.

`projectedFile` drops every section headed `## Work Log` until the next heading of level 2 or higher. A second, invented `## Work Log` heading placed anywhere in an audit ticket body would therefore exempt that body text from binding. Frontmatter scope fields stay bound, and only a trusted local author could do this, so it is not blocking. Exempting only the first or final Work Log section, or refusing duplicates, would close it.

Because the reader hash covers almost every tracked file (docs, tests, website), every commit touching those files must refresh `audit-readers.json`. Until it is refreshed, Work Log and status updates make observations stale. This is conservative and documented, but it adds friction: a stale policy fails closed without being noticed.
